doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

chapter: Selling the store and founding Evidence
title: Wanting musical input as a label owner
summary: Gordon says label owners want input because labels extend themselves; taste mattered more than money.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Did you feel inclined to have musical input, the fact that you were sort of footing the bill?

Absolutely. Doesn’t everybody with money who starts a record label? They all want to have input. You know because the labels are extensions of themselves. And so many Indy record label owners — money was certainly not their primary concern, it was to develop a label of taste, a label of hipness you know, a label of coolness. So sure I wanted to have input.
